controls.basis: a relative difference of 0.5 against a tolerance of 1e-12 is arithmetic; and an edge whose weight is 0.0 is not carrying weight, which is the definition the gate semantics give, not one this tool supplies
controls.control: a numeric difference exceeds tolerance AND a dead edge reads as a different decision

controls.basis: a value equals itself and a set equals itself; both follow from the definitions of equality, not from this tool
controls.control: identical values differ by zero AND identical gate maps read as the same decision

instrument_controls.does_not_establish: that the instrument's other measurements are correct. A control pair shows it still responds to a known stimulus and stays silent on a null one -- it is a liveness and discrimination check, not a calibration.

note: Bit identity is NOT demanded where the platform contract does not guarantee it. The four outcomes are reported separately so a numerical difference is never read as a decision failure, and a decision failure is never excused as rounding.

runs.alignment_note: EXACT_LAYER_TICK_INDEX joins on the live layer's own tick boundary, so a compared pair is the same tick by construction. NEAREST_WALL_CLOCK_WITHIN_HALF_TICK matches on wall time, which advances at ~0.0407 s per tick against the layer's 0.0400 s, so the pair need not be the same tick. Results obtained under the two alignments are NOT comparable.
runs.fidelity_note: The hand-off reconstruction now keys on channel ARRIVAL TIME, which is what the live adapter's freshness gate does. The earlier reconstruction compared VALUES and so missed 58.8% of hand-offs on a committed log, because two identical consecutive readings looked like no new reading (HF-010). That removed most of the ArduPilot divergence -- 511 categorical differences fell to 13 -- and left PX4 unchanged at 144, so what remains on PX4 has a DIFFERENT cause. HF-014 has now attributed the MECHANISM and not the root cause: all 144 are the replay seeing MORE live edges than the recording (never fewer), 122 of them exactly `altitude_baro`, and every affected edge is one whose weight is a product of per-sensor FRESHNESS terms while the residual values agree. A single differing staleness timeout was tested as the explanation and RULED OUT. HF-017 THEN FOUND THE CAUSE, AND IT WAS THIS TOOL. The divergence was an artifact of pairing a replayed state with the recorded row NEAREST IN WALL TIME: the replay carries the layer's exact tick grid, the recording was shifted by its first row's t_mono, and on the log in question that shift was 0.59 of a tick. Joining on the layer's own tick index instead gives 0 divergent and 2250 of 2250 bit-identical on the same log, with ArduPilot unchanged at 0. WHAT THAT DOES NOT MEAN. It does not close HF-004: two SITL runs replaying without a categorical divergence is not a general property of the instrument, and the software-hardening gate must not read it as one. A numeric residual also remains, accumulating through the alpha/beta recursion to 6.7e-10, which is above the declared 1e-12 tolerance; the tolerance has not been changed to accommodate it.
